name: Brennick Carryout Bag Ordinance
enacted: nine months before the effective date

source_sentences: From the effective date, all retailers in Brennick are prohibited from providing single-use plastic carryout bags (plastic bags with handles, thinner than 4 mil (0.1 mm)) at the point of sale.
Exempt are bags without handles for produce, meat and bulk goods inside the store, pharmacy prescription bags, and restaurant takeout bags.
The neighboring town of Fallow Creek has no bag rules; two large supermarkets there are within 1 km of the city line on Route 9, close to several Brennick neighborhoods.
The ordinance was passed nine months before it took effect.
The City Office of Sustainability enforces the ordinance on a complaint-driven basis: a written warning, then fines of $100, $250 and $500 per day of violation.
Enforcement is funded from the general budget.
Recycled-paper carryout bags may be provided only for a charge of at least 10 cents a bag, kept by the retailer and shown on the receipt.
Reusable bags (designed for at least 125 uses; at least 4 mil if plastic) may be sold at any price.
Customers paying with food-assistance benefits receive paper bags free.

unclear.text: how a bag's design for 125 uses is verified
readings: U1-a: a maker's claim is accepted, since the ordinance sets no test

context: Retailers there have given away thin plastic carryout bags at the checkout, at a cost to them of about 2 cents a bag, built into their prices.
Surveys suggest that about 60% of households reuse some of them as bin liners or for pet waste.
